_source: HCM 7th Edition, Chapter 32, TWSC Example Problem 2: pedestrian crossing at a TWSC intersection. Four-lane major street, 1,700 veh/h bidirectional peak hour, K-factor 0.08, walking speed 4.0 ft/s, start-up and end clearance 1.0 s, no pedestrian platooning. Three scenarios share these facts and differ only in crossing staging, countermeasures, and motorist yield rate: A is a 46-ft unmarked single-stage crossing of all four lanes with a 0% yield rate; B and C are two-stage crossings of 20 ft and two lanes per stage, with half the volume (850 veh/h) conflicting at each stage, a marked crosswalk and median refuge, and yield rates of 50% and 80% respectively. C adds RRFBs. Scenario keys map to the PedestrianCrossing schema of src/hcm/twsc/pedestrian.rs.
